Recent research supports informative negatives while warning that maximum-score mining can amplify false negatives. [Hard-BPR (2024 preprint; 2025 publication)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) modifies the pairwise ranking objective to mitigate false negatives under dynamic hard sampling; its evidence concerns implicit collaborative filtering, so transfer to masked BERT4Rec remains unverified. [CATS (SIGIR 2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) adaptively samples across item clusters, proposing that positives’ own clusters contain more false negatives and neighboring clusters offer useful hard negatives. Neither establishes gains on these four RecHarness categories.

Sampling bias and false-negative contamination are distinct problems. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compares random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling, finding dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity trade-offs. [Sampled Estimators for Softmax Must Be Biased (NeurIPS 2025)](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/42b7c2f6d320d1fe1afa899a6319d6d7-Abstract-Conference.html) shows that subset-only softmax estimators necessarily retain bias under its framework; sampling correction should therefore not be described as eliminating bias or identifying false negatives.

Experimental implication, rather than an established result: retain masked-target BERT4Rec and compare uniform sampled cross-entropy against a warm-started mixture of uniform and same-network-mined negatives, excluding known training positives. Test moderate-hardness selection or a small Hard-BPR auxiliary term to limit pressure from extreme candidates. Any sampling correction must reflect the actual sampling procedure; deterministic top-k mining cannot simply inherit uniform correction. Use one jointly trained checkpoint per category, appended-mask inference, and unchanged macro validation HR@10 to determine whether Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific benefit.
